headline: Fuel prices rise by Tk 20 per litre across the board in Bangladesh
summary: The price hike in diesel, petrol, octane, and kerosene will likely trigger a domino effect on food and transport costs, hitting low-income households the hardest.
details: Bangladesh has seen a Tk 20 per litre increase in the price of diesel, petrol, octane, and kerosene. This hike comes amid already high inflation and weak private investment.

The immediate concern is the 'second-round effects' where higher fuel costs spread through transport, food, agriculture, and industry. The government has not yet clearly explained how it will contain these inflationary pressures.

Diesel is particularly critical as it powers irrigation, generators, and freight. Higher diesel prices typically lead to increased freight charges and bus and truck operating costs, which are then passed on to consumers.

Food inflation is expected to be sensitive because transport and irrigation costs rise simultaneously. This can lead to a been persistent inflation that is harder to reverse once businesses adjust prices.

The impact will be regressive, hitting poorer households more severely. They spend a larger share of their income on food and transport, meaning a modest increase in fares or food prices will significantly lower their living standards.
While the government cannot shield consumers from global oil price shocks indefinitely, experts suggest the need for a transparent pricing rule and a review of the tax structure on fuel.

Higher energy costs also squeeze business margins, especially for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that have less capacity to absorb shocks. This could lead to delayed investment and weakened employment creation.
To protect the vulnerable, the government is urged to provide targeted support for low-income households, agriculture, and essential public transport rather than indiscriminate subsidies.

headline: 4 rail staff suspended after RU students vandalise Rajshahi station
summary: Thousands of Rajshahi University students protested and vandalised the railway station after a fellow student was allegedly assaulted by rail security forces.
details: Thousands of Rajshahi University (RU) students vandalised the Rajshahi Railway Station and blocked rail lines on Sunday night. The unrest broke out after a student from the Department of Islamic History, Ayub Ali, was allegedly assaulted by rail security forces.

The protest, led by RUCSU GS Saluddin Ammar, saw students using sticks to attack and damage station property. Panic ensued among passengers waiting for trains, including the Dhumketu Express, as students stormed the station.

The situation escalated further when local political activists joined the scene, leading to clashes and stone-pelting between students and locals. The unrest continued until around 3:30 AM when university and local administration officials intervened.

In response to the incident, railway authorities have suspended four rail employees. A four-member committee has also been formed by Western Railway to investigate the causes of the assault and the subsequent violence.

University officials and the local administration worked together to clear the students from the station and ensure the safety of the detained rail employees. Rail communication has since returned to normal.
